EU-001.note: Six of the eight utility-catalog entries are reachable. The Tools command group registers pick-colour, hash-checker, icon-converter, video-converter and qr-code, each opening one non-modal owned dialog, and image-comparer is reachable from the editor through the compare-images command. The video converter is present only where XERAHS_RECORDING and GStreamer with pbutils are found; on a build without GStreamer the command and its dialog are absent rather than explained at the start surface. background-remover is not implemented and has no approved platform disposition. konami-shader stays inventoried in the contract catalog with disposition product-owner-decision-required and has no native implementation, which is what EU-019 requires until the owner decides. A missing host service is explained rather than fatal: a missing desktop portal and a denied permission are distinct outcomes and the colour picker shows a visible message instead of crashing. Unconditional reachability of every catalog entry and the video converter availability policy remain Required.

audit.coverage: Candidate production/test seams exist; the full normative behavior is not established. See the capability audit remaining_scope and row note; no completion is inferred from test presence.

EU-002.note: Capture permission is owned by the native desktop portal: the picker issues one xdg-desktop-portal ColorPicker request at a time and distinguishes Picked, Cancelled, Denied and Failed, with a missing portal distinct from a permission denial. The picked colour is presented in eight canonical formats (Hex, HexAlpha, Rgb, Rgba, Hsb, Hsl, Cmyk and Decimal) and a hex field is parsed and re-formatted. Copy happens only on an explicit user action: a per-line Copy, a Copy All that stays disabled until a colour is shown, and no automatic clipboard write; an invalid hex keeps the last valid colour. Keyboard cancellation uses the native QDialog reject path and a portal cancellation leaves the shown colour and message unchanged. The sampled area is not magnified and the sampled coordinates are not exposed, because the portal returns a colour alone. Magnification and coordinates remain Required.

EU-003.note: The encoder validates its input and produces typed failures: empty content and over-long content are refused, an invalid output size is refused, and the Reed-Solomon divisor, remainder, format information bits, version bits and capacity table are checked against hand-computed and published vectors. The render is deterministic, and the scannability oracle decodes the rendered PNG with zbarimg across every error-correction level and several versions, including UTF-8 content and capacity boundaries. The window supports explicit Copy to the clipboard, Save to a PNG written atomically through a temporary sibling, and Upload through a host-supplied port that receives an existing PNG path; the uploaded PNG lives in the dialog's own temporary directory and is removed with the dialog. A missing upload port leaves the action unavailable rather than failing.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-004.note: QR scanning is not implemented. There is no QR decoder in the native tree: the qr-scan entry in the Core post-capture action catalog is a declared action specification only and is not a scanner. The Screen, Region and Image File modes, capture and file consent, input validation and limits, and the distinct zero, one and multiple decoded results do not exist, and no sampled pixels are uploaded because no pixels are sampled. QR scanning remains Required.

EU-005.note: The hash checker offers CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 and selects SHA-256 by default. Files are read in 1 MiB chunks, so a digest does not grow the reader's memory, and the known digests of an empty and a non-empty file are checked against published values and a large file matches a one-shot hash. Progress reports the bytes hashed and the file size, with an indeterminate bar when the size is unknown, and cancellation is polled at every chunk boundary so a cancelled read reports cancelled instead of a partial digest. digestMatches compares every digit and does not stop at the first difference, so the result does not depend on where two values parted; the length check is safe because the length follows from the algorithm.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-006.note: A result names its algorithm and the file it came from, and the digest is presented as lowercase hexadecimal. hashAlgorithmIsWeak marks CRC32, MD5 and SHA-1 as unsuitable for security verification, and the hash checker labels a weak choice as unsuitable for security; nothing recommends MD5 or SHA-1 for an authenticity decision.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-007.note: The converter validates the source image and refuses an invalid or oversized one with a visible error. It offers the six contract sizes 16, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 and both an 8-bit palette and a 32-bit true-color mode, and Save stays disabled until at least one size is checked. The container writer produces a structurally valid .ico: the header and every directory entry are well formed, a true-color entry keeps its alpha and a palette entry carries the expected header and mask, and the written file is read back and accepted by Qt's own 32-bit container reader. A cancelled save writes nothing, and a missing size list, an invalid size, an invalid image and a write failure each have their own stable code.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-008.note: Two independent validated images are loaded; a top-left comparison uses independently expected pixels and a centred alignment uses native sizes with odd padding, and invalid inputs and an over-large union fail before any allocation. Size and format incompatibility is reported rather than silently accepted. The before/after divider is exposed through native accessibility and is operable by keyboard and by drag, the divider endpoints preserve alpha and show exactly one source, and unsupported visible objects and a cancelled rendering leave both inputs untouched. Neither image is modified, saved or uploaded, and the comparison owns its rendered snapshot.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-012.note: The converter exposes the 15 codec choices of the utility catalog in catalog order, each with its compatible containers, encoder candidates, hardware flag and bitrate property, and VideoConversionTest checks the catalogue against the contract. The window offers the input file, the output folder and name, the bitrate where it is meaningful, progress, Cancel and an optional open-folder action, and the list, validation and success flows are tested. The whole utility is conditional on the build: the converter library is compiled only when XERAHS_RECORDING and GStreamer with pbutils are found, so on a target without GStreamer the command and its dialog are absent rather than offered and explained. Unconditional availability across the supported desktop targets remains Required.

audit.coverage: Candidate production/test seams exist; the full normative behavior is not established. See the capability audit remaining_scope and row note; no completion is inferred from test presence.

EU-013.note: codecAvailability never substitutes another codec: an unusable codec carries an actionable reason and the dialog lists it as disabled, so a hardware codec is shown only when it is usable. Command arguments are structured rather than built as a string: the pipeline description is path-free and names only src, dec, mux and sink, and the runner sets the filesrc and filesink location as a structured property, so a path cannot be injected into a command line. Output is written atomically to a hidden partial sibling next to the target and renamed only on success. The encoded argument is the structured properties of the plan, which is checked for the audio encoder and its dropped-audio diagnostic.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-014.note: planConversion validates the container, codec and input combination and every invalid pair is rejected before a pipeline is built. The output rules never allow the input to be its own output and refuse an existing file unless overwrite is explicitly opted in, and suggestOutputPath reserves a non-conflicting name beside the input. The input file is preserved. A cancelled conversion removes the incomplete output, and the host result distinguishes Success, Cancelled and Failed through a dedicated outcome plus a stable error code. An existing output is refused rather than overwritten by default.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-015.note: Utility inputs stay on the device. The hash checker reads the file and keeps only its digest; the colour picker keeps a recent-colour list inside the dialog; the image comparison owns a rendered snapshot and does not modify, save or upload either input. The one outward path is the QR Upload action, which is an explicit user action handing a PNG path to the host's own file-upload port, and the uploaded PNG lives in the dialog's temporary directory and is removed with the dialog. Diagnostics are stable codes without paths or content.

audit.coverage: Tested candidate behavior in the cited production/test surfaces and published vectors where supplied. Supported-target/human activation remains a separate gate.

EU-016.note: The utility windows use native Qt controls with accessible names, visible focus and keyboard traversal: the image comparison exposes an accessible divider operable by keyboard and drag, the QR controls are named for accessibility, and the video converter's failure state carries a stable code with accessible names. Busy and error states are descriptive rather than silent, Cancel and close have defined semantics, file selection uses the native file dialog and capture uses the native desktop portal. High-contrast rendering is not exercised by a test on this platform, and the all-platforms clause is not evidenced here, so high-contrast and cross-platform accessibility qualification remain Required.
